# HFlow

> Read-only sequential and parallel workflow stages with native scrolling and node selection.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.10.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HFlow` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-flow>`.
- Constructor: `HearthFlowElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Diagrams.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HFlow.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- A read-only sequence/parallel workflow, not an arbitrary graph editor. Each parallel entry is a branch containing another sequence. Native lists, node buttons and CSS connectors preserve document order. Narrow containers stack stages; larger diagrams scroll natively. select emits a stage ID; selected is application-owned. Cycles/depth/excess nodes are omitted with a notice. Defaults: maxNodes=200, maxDepth=6.

## Public API

items: FlowStage[] · label, selected: string · orientation: horizontal | vertical · maxNodes, maxDepth: number

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    items: FlowStage[];
    label: string;
    selected?: string;
    orientation?: "horizontal" | "vertical";
    maxNodes?: number;
    maxDepth?: number;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ items: () => [], orientation: "horizontal", maxNodes: 200, maxDepth: 6 }
```

### Events

select(string)

```ts
type Emits = {
    select: [
        id: string
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

footer

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, viewport, node

Use `hearth-flow::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export interface FlowStage {
    id: string;
    label: string;
    description?: string;
    status?: RunStatus;
    parallel?: FlowStage[][];
}

export type RunStatus = "pending" | "running" | "success" | "error" | "skipped";
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HFlow } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';
const stages = [{id:'fetch',label:'Fetch',status:'success' as const},{id:'checks',label:'Checks',status:'running' as const,parallel:[[{id:'test',label:'Test',status:'running' as const}],[{id:'lint',label:'Lint',status:'success' as const}]]},{id:'deploy',label:'Deploy',status:'pending' as const}];
</script>

<template>
  <HFlow label="Build workflow" :items="stages" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-flow');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Build workflow",
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "fetch",
      "label": "Fetch",
      "status": "success"
    },
    {
      "id": "checks",
      "label": "Checks",
      "status": "running",
      "parallel": [
        [
          {
            "id": "test",
            "label": "Test",
            "status": "running"
          }
        ],
        [
          {
            "id": "lint",
            "label": "Lint",
            "status": "success"
          }
        ]
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "deploy",
      "label": "Deploy",
      "status": "pending"
    }
  ]
});

element.addEventListener('select', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```
